items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Well, I played a few dates with Piku. I played with him in a little town in Louisiana.

ctx.x: Yeah, their father was a famous old time bass too.

Yes, he was. I never heard of him. Same way as Bob Rand's daddy. He's an old time... He died last year. Yeah, I understand he did. In June. He had a big funeral. Yes, I understand he did. And so with Piku, I... Well, that was the biggest in history almost. Yes. Well, I played a few dates with Piku. I played with him in a little town in Louisiana. We called it the De La Cua Islands.
Oh yes, down there. Way down in the bottom.

You take like Blanton that was with Duke that died so young, well Blanton could make his bass sound like a shallow. And those are the things that a lot of musicians don't know how to get tonations out of their horns. You know the smart playing. It's not what we call a pinch tone, it's a round tone, it's big. And a lot of musicians in those days, the first thing they did, they studied their tonations. Like Big Al Loy, Lil Nelson, beautiful tone. Piku, tonation. Or listen to Bonnie's tone.
Well a lot of guys had to work in the street and I think that you have to develop strength and tone and everything there.
